projects.title: Lake House
projects.summary: A quiet concrete pavilion shaped by water, horizon and the changing edge of the landscape.
projects.statement: The project is organized as a sequence of sheltered rooms opening toward the lake. A restrained material palette keeps attention on light, proportion and the landscape beyond.
projects.longView: Durability, shade and a measured relationship to water.

projects.title: Woodland House
projects.summary: A compact house composed around a protected courtyard and a continuous relationship with the trees.
projects.statement: Deep thresholds frame the woodland and give each room a distinct degree of privacy. The courtyard becomes the center of daily life and the reference point for movement through the house.
projects.longView: A compact footprint organized around light, privacy and daily life.

projects.title: Cantilever Residence
projects.summary: A layered residence where a precise upper volume creates shade, shelter and long framed views.
projects.statement: The upper level extends beyond the lower stone base to form a generous covered terrace. Interior spaces follow the same linear order, moving from enclosed service rooms to open living areas.
projects.longView: Deep shade and durable transitions for a changing coastal climate.

projects.title: Río Segundo Commons
projects.summary: A mixed-use district study that brings homes, work, hospitality and everyday services into a more connected urban edge.
projects.statement: The project begins with the relationship between a working street, a shaded public threshold and a flexible mix of uses. Its early framework asks how a district can grow in phases while keeping daily life connected.
projects.longView: Adaptable uses, connected daily life and a clear public edge over time.

projects.title: Golfo Dulce Retreat
projects.summary: A hospitality destination shaped by arrival, rest and a close reading of the forested coast.
projects.statement: The destination is conceived as a sequence of sheltered rooms, shared spaces and landscape thresholds that keep the coast present without competing with it. Operations, seasonality and the character of the site guide the first development decisions.
projects.longView: A durable guest experience shaped by landscape, seasonality and stewardship.

projects.title: Coyol Free Zone Campus
projects.summary: A logistics and employment campus conceived around movement, adaptability and a clear relationship to the Alajuela corridor.
projects.statement: The campus is planned as an expandable framework rather than a single object: productive buildings, shared services and a landscape structure that keeps future phases legible.
projects.longView: A flexible platform for investment, employment and long-term operations.

projects.title: Central Valley Corporate Campus
projects.summary: A corporate campus study that brings work, landscape and shared services into a more adaptable daily setting.
projects.statement: The campus is structured as a sequence of shaded courtyards, shared amenities and flexible work buildings. Its framework supports changing teams and uses while keeping movement through the site clear.
projects.longView: A durable work setting with room for changing teams, uses and mobility.

projects.title: Guanacaste Coastal District
projects.summary: A master-planned coastal district study balancing hospitality, services, landscape and the long horizon of a growing region.
projects.statement: The district begins with the relationship between dry forest, arrival routes and a sequence of shared civic and hospitality spaces. Early planning keeps the landscape structure visible as future phases take shape.
projects.longView: A measured transition between landscape, hospitality, services and daily life.
